cells.date: Makara of the year with Jupiter in Karkataka.
cells.remarks: Records a gift of 35 kalañju of gold for burning a perpetual lamp in the temple of Devadana Tiruvadi at Tirunelli by a certain Kodai Iramanayan of Valluva-nadu. The devamarmis of Nelkkun-gam, including the Panduravaraiyar, received the gold and undertook to provide for the burning of the lamp by commuting its interest in paddy into that of oil from the residents of Ilam-bilaiyur.

cells.remarks: Gift of 16 veli of land free of taxes in Nelur newly constituted into a brahmadeya village called Paijaltamangalam to a number of Brahmanas ashtabhogatejas of Mahabalidaram. This included the 12 veli of land already granted as brahmadeya in the 59th year of the king. The ajnapti was Vijaya-nallujan of Alappakkam. The engraver of these plates was Sci Dandi, son of Videlividugu Pallavapparadsachchen of Aimbaniaocheri of Kaohohippädu.

cells.remarks: Records the gift of the village Drujjavaram surnamed as Aṇavēmapura on the banks of the river Malapaha in the Kurtiḍēśa by the king, to the brāhmaṇ Appayārya who was the purohita of the king and to his three brothers Śrīrāma-Bhaṭṭa, Pinnaya-Bhaṭṭa and Sōma-Bhaṭṭa. These were the sons of Allada-Bhaṭṭa and belonged to the Śrīvatsa-gōtra. Pinnaya-Bhaṭṭa is said to have been the king's adviser on Dharmas (i.e., law).

cells.remarks: Registers a gift of land in Marudūr in Urattūr-kōṭṭam to two individuals (mentioned in No. 354, above) of Vikrama-śōḷa-chaturvēdimangalam in Ēriyūr-nāḍu, a subdivision of Paṇḍikōḷapati-vaḷanāḍu, for offerings to the god Tirumālīśvaram-uḍaiya-Nāyaṇār at Vēmbāṇūr for the prosperity of the country. Mābeḷi-Vāṇarāyar is herein called the son (piḷḷai) of Sōmanātha-dēvar.

[date-calculation appendix, No. 448: Saka 1370 (wrong), Prajapati expired, Angirasa, Rishabha, su. dvadasi, Sunday, Hasta, Vaigasi 4 = A.D. 1452, April 3, Sunday ; 89; 55. cells.remarks: Registers gift of the village Kajakēśarīpuram alias Pāpa-nāśam with all the taxes levied on the village, for offerings, worship, twilight lamps etc., and for conducting the festivals instituted in the temple of Pāpanāśam-Perumāḷ. cells.remarks: Registars an agreement made among the 'Vaḷaiyūr (kōma-munity) of Southern Ceylon that they would collect 2 kāśu from individual living at Tirukkannapuram and other places, for maintaining the temple and other purposes. The maṭha called Soḍukar Karuṇākara-vīrar-maḍam, where Śrī-Vaishnavas were to be fed on all festival occasions. The present record is stated to have been engraved in place of an old one which had disappeared.

cells.remarks: Begins with the introduction "பூமலர் வளர" etc. Registers a royal order creating a brahmadeya village called Kulasekhara-chaturvedimangalam by grouping together four devadana villages and granting them with lands and Vedas and the Sastras on the representation of Kalingarayar. The order was issued while the king was occupying the seat called Kalingarayan in his palace (koyil) at Madura to the east of Madakkulam in Maduradaya-valanadu.

cells.remarks: Gift of taxes on two pieces of land belonging to the temple of Tiruttaṅgal, at Śrīpaṇḍāra-chaturvēdimangalam, a brāhmaṇa in Iruñjōṇāḍu by the assembly of that place, including land already granted to the temple by Śōḷu yāṇvaḍa-dēva, a brāhmaṇa of Aṇḍanārkōḍi in Puṅga-nāḍu, who is stated to have colonised the village by order of the king and to whom the assembly had granted the income thereon.

cells.remarks: States that Tiruttaṇgal Chē-iṉmā was the gift for blood-shed (ra-ttakkāri) to Ullibommaṉ Kālaṅgadagaṇda-Nāyakkar, the follower of Vaṟatūṅgarat-Tainpalli Kaḻaṅgadagaṇda-Nāyakkar. Adjacent to the inscription is the figure of a standing warrior whose sword has almost cut off the head of a horse on whose back is seated another warrior with a sword. By the side of the hero is another inscribed stone slab.

cells.date: Chāḷukya-Vikrama year 15, Prajāpati, Kārtika amāvāsye, Sunday.
cells.remarks: Records gifts of lands made at the villages Siruguppe, Siriyūru and Kōlaṇuru to the god Svayambhū-Kēdāra-varadēva of Siruguppu, by Abhinayavarasetti Piriya-Kētaḷadēvi, the queen of Tribhuvanamalla-dēva, for the merit of the queen. Mention is made of the temple servants. It is also stated that the 'Sindu family who was the lord of Bhogāvatipura, made provision for feeding brahmans. The queen is stated to have been governing the said villages, which were situated in the subdivision Tekke-Kāṇaya.

cells.date: Śāka 980, Havilambi, Vaisākha śu. puppami, Thursday, Vyatīpāta, lunar eclipse. [date-calculation appendix, No. 677: Śaka 980, Hēvalambi, Vaiśākha, śu. paurṇami, Thursday, Vyatipāta, Lunar eclipse. In Śaka 980, Hēvalambi = A.D. 1057, there was a Lunar eclipse on Sunday, 23rd March in the month of Chaitra and not in Vaiśākha as cited in the inscription. The given details seem to be erroneous in more than one respect.]
cells.remarks: Registers the gift of the three villages Duddhiyāla, Siripu...and Kurukunide respectively to the temple of Svayambhu-Bhuvanēśvara, Saraiśagēvarēdeva and Indrēsvaradeva at the western entrance to the Śrīsaila. The gift was made into the hands of Suradēva-Nāyaka by the king and his chief queen Mailādēvi, for the merit of the chief of the temple at Maḷikārjuna at 'Ia'[Ya]lni at the western entrance to Śrīsaila. Mentions the chief Ballavarassa and the village Mōsaṇgi.

cells.location: Anantasayanaguḍi
cells.place: On the east wall of the maṇḍapa of the Anantasayanasvāmin temple
cells.date: Śaka 1471, Saumya, 'Paushya, du. 9, Uttarāyaṇa-saṁkrānti. [date-calculation appendix, No. 682: Śaka 1471, Saumya, Pushya, śu. 9, Makara-Saṁkrānti = A.D. 1549, December 28, Saturday; ·60. The nak. Aśvini was current till ·24 of the day.]
cells.remarks: Gives the genealogy of the second Vijayanagara dynasty up to Krishṇarāya, similar to that in copper-plate records. States that the king founded the town of Sūle-Tirumala-Mahārājapuram wherein he built a temple for the god Anantapadmanābha, that he made a gift of several villages in the Pāṇḍya-nādu which was a subdivision of the kingdom of Vijayanagara, for worship and offerings in the temple and that he appointed sers (sthānīka) of the aiyyaṅkāra-nasa seent for conducting the worship of the god. The inscription is stated to be the composition of the poet Ṣaḍākshari.

cells.date: Śaka 1467, Viśvā-vasu, Chaitra, śu. 3, Thursday. [date-calculation appendix, No. 697: Saka 1440 (expired), Bahudhanya, Karttika, su. 12, Saturday. Probably A.D. 1518, October 15, Friday ; 84. N.B.—The week-day quoted in the inscription is apparently wrong by a day; but probably the date has to be interpreted in the light of some local rule regarding the keeping of ekadasi. For instance, it will be seen from page 57 Ind. Eph., Vol. I, part 1, that if on ekadasi day there is any part of navami or dasami, then the Vaishnava rule is to keep ekadasi on dvadasi day. Actually in the year in question (Ind. Eph., Vol. V, page 239), Thursday, 14 October, on which the tithi su. 11 ended at 91 of the day was properly a day of dasami (ended at 00 of day) and according to the above rule, ekadasi may have been kept on Friday and dvadasi on Saturday (L.D.S.)]

States that the king founded the town of Sūle-Tirumala-Mahārājapuram wherein he built a temple for the god Anantapadmanābha, that he made a gift of several villages in the Pāṇḍya-nādu which was a subdivision of the kingdom of Vijayanagara, for worship and offerings in the temple and that he appointed sers (sthānīka) of the aiyyaṅkāra-nasa seat for conducting the worship of the god. cells.place: On the Nandi-pillar planted before the Amarēśvara temple in the same village (as Kēśavasvāmin temple). †
cells.language: Sanskrit (prose and verse) in Telugu and Telugu.
cells.remarks: Purports to record the grant of the village Lavanapura (Upputuru) to 1,000 brāhmaṇas who were the followers of Yajñavalkya and who are said to take their descent from the town Ahōhatrapura on the banks of the Ganges, by Trinētra-Pallava. Also records the measurements of the streets called Rōmavīdhi and Sūryavīdhi as well as the house-sites that were presented and the garden and the arable lands allotted to each share. It also records certain agreements made between the shareholders as selling shares in the village to outsiders and receiving dowries for girls in marriage. Separate shares were allotted to the gods Mahādēva, Kēdāra and Vighnēśvara and the goddess Padāmbikāśakti. The extent of the village and its boundaries are given. For genealogy and minute details, See C. P. No. 8 of Appendix A above.

cells.remarks: Damaged. Records a grant of land made to the temples of Bhīmēśvar, Gōpmatha and Vighnēśvara to the scholars of Paruchūru by Inkolani Tirumala-Reddi. The grant is said to have been in the nāyankara of the chief and attached to the Adḍanki-āvaḍi. The grant was made for the merit of his father, his mother, his brother, his paternal uncle Srigiri-Reddi, his mother Annadēvi. The chief is also said to have granted some land to the temple of the god Maḍḍukēśvara on the banks of the Guṇḍlakamma.

cells.location: Idupulapādu
cells.place: On the four faces of the Garuda-pillar planted near the dhvaja-stambha of the Chēnnakēśavasvāmin temple
cells.language: Sanskrit verse and Telugu and Telugu verse.
cells.remarks: Records the grant, by the king, who was the son of Paru-shōttama and grandson of Kapilēśvara, of the village called Idupulapādu to the schola-mādhavas of the Bhā-radvāja-gōtra. The genealogy of the king as well as that of the donee is given. The ancestors of the donee for three previous generations appear to have been scholars. Two previous generations appear to have been familiar with the Kāya-yāna-sūtra and the Kanva-śākhā. The name of the village Idupulapādu in Kāna-rāshṭra made by Trinayana-Pallava to Brāhmaṇas of various gōtras who were learned in the Vedas and there were the followers of the Kātyāyana-sūtra and the Kanva-śākhā. The names of the donces and their respective shares are enumerated.

cells.date: Śaka 1536, Ānanda, Meesha su. 3, Saturday, Rohiṇī. [date-calculation appendix, No. 94: Saka 1586, Ananda, Masha, éu. 8, Saturday, Rohini = A.D. 1614, April 2, Saturday, ‘27; f.d.n. 36.]
cells.remarks: Engraved in continuation of the previous inscription Records the repairs executed by Lekshmaṇ Kuṁara Tatāchārya to the Puṇyakōṭimāna originally erected by Kṛishṇaiya and which had become dilapidated, the construction of the Kalyāṇakoṭimāna, gifting it with gold, the gift of cows, and the rebuilding of the maṇḍapa, the gōpura and the prākāra of the ammana-śhrine, and built-in. Registers the provision made for celebrating the festivals on the first day of each month (māsappirappu) and on Amāvāsya days in the temple of Saṅjīvarāya (i.e. Hanumān) by the merchants of various countries who were present at Tālasamudram on the occasion of the consecration of the image, in the cyolio year Subhākṛit, Aṇi, payō’s-iṣhta, Anūsha, Kanyā-lagnæ, Monday. Mentions Chempagattaraiyar. (Damaged).

cells.place: On the other side of the slab of Agastīśvara temple †
cells.remarks: States that Mahārāja Rāja Śrī Liṅgōji Saṅgaru-Mahāsaya who was governing the entire Karṇāṭa country renovated the temples of Ekāmbaranāhasvāmī, Kamākshīdēvi and Kachchhapēśvarasvāmī at Śiva-Kāñchī and of Varadā-rājasvāmī, established many Brāhmaṇa (agrahāras) and founded tanks and groves, and in that connection widened the tank at Puṭṭūr and built a sluice for it. He had a new channel dug from the Palāru river to this tank and provided for supplying the water therefrom to many villages on the east of the tank.

cells.remarks: Begins with the introduction 'Svasti śrî', etc. Stones missing. Seems to register a gift of land for two perpetual lamps in the temple of Tiruvi-Vinnagara-Âlvâr by queen Trailôkyamahadēvi, one on behalf of her mother Umangai and the other on behalf of Vikramaśôsari Pallavaraiyar. Mentions the liquid measure Arumolidēvan. Incomplete. Begins with the introduction 'Svasti śrî', etc. Registers a gift by purchase of a top and land made tax-free, for offerings to the god Tiruvira- Vīngar-Ālvār in the name of the queen Sembiyan Mukkôkkilānļigal alias Kannara Nächchi Pidāranangai by a certain Araiyan Kōdāran of Papivanganga- nallur in the Chola country. Mentions the liquid measure 'Sōliyan'. cells.place: On the wall of Mahā-munīśvara temple †
cells.remarks: Begins with the introduction "Pugalum ōngu," etc. Records an order of the great assembly of Rājēndrasōla- chaturvēdimangalam (i.e. Ucliramērūr), an independent village in Kaliyūr-kōttam, a subdivision of Jayangonda- sōla-mandalam, remitting the taxes on 30 padāgam of land purchased by Araiyan Gangaikondan alias Sola- vichādarap-Pallavaraiyar of Iraiyur in Pandikulasani- valanādu, a subdivision of Sōla-mandalam, and granted by him along with the house-site with the money given by Tiru-maligai-Vallal and Vippur-Sundan-Dēvan for the maintenance of a matha called Arulaladāsan which he had founded. The land was lying fallow for 60 or 70 years and was now called Solavichohadīra-vilāgam after the donor. The tax on the land was exempted for the current (46th) year, but for the years following five kāśu per annum was to be levied on the land. Other taxes such as pidagai-vari, uppu-kāśu etc., were remitted altogether.

cells.date: 16th year, Tulā, śu. Paurṇami, Uttarēś, Rēvati, Saturday. [date-calculation appendix, No. 213: 6th year, Dhanus, śu. daśami, Rōhiṇi = A.D. 1344, Dec. 13, Monday. The tithis śu. 7 and śu. 8 were both current on this day and the latter ended at ·95 of the day. The tithi quoted in the inscription is perhaps a mistake. The nak. Rōhiṇi commenced at ·47 on Monday and ended at ·45 the next day.]
cells.remarks: Gift of 8 cows for a lamp and offerings, to the same temple.

cells.place: On the left side of the entrance into the gopura of Dakshiṇāmūrti shrine. †
cells.date: 6th year, Dhanus, daśamī, Rōhiṇī, Monday, Rōhiṇī. Śaka 1348, Visu-vasu, Kanya, śu. pañchami, Wed-nesday, Uttarām. [date-calculation appendix, No. 214: Saka 1348, Visvavasu, Kanya, su. panchami, Wednesday, Uttiram. Su. 5 and nak. Uttiram cannot combine in the month of Kanya. The given details are irregular. Mallikarjunadeva-Maharaya, son of Virapratapa Devaraya-Maharaya, ‘who instituted the elephant hunt.’]
cells.remarks: Registers an order of Salākāya-Nāyakkar, the agent of mahāpradhāni Mallarasa-Uḍaiyār to the weavers of Uttaramerūr alias Rājēndrachōlapuram, to make over oles (records) of tax-free land which was a tirunamattakkāni of the temple, fixing the total amount of the taxes on the several professions to be paid annually to the temple.

cells.place: On a stone excavated below the Cathedral at San Thomé, Madras.
cells.date: 6th year, Dhanus, daśamī, Rōhiṇī, Monday, Rōhiṇī. Śaka 1348, Visu-vasu, Kanya, śu. pañchami, Wed-nesday, Uttarām.
cells.remarks: Fragment. In characters of about the 12th century A.D. Seems to register a tax-free gift of land for burning a twilight lamp before the image of Kuṭṭākkuṇḍavar (Kriṭṭākkuṇḍarāja) in the temple of Niruṇyā(r)l-nā[r]y-ana(r)l. Contains a portion of the historics introduction of the king commencing with "Pūgagal-mādu", etc., and stops with the mention of the king's name.
